beats.text: Five final lines that readers never forget.
"So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past." — The Great Gatsby.
"It is a far, far better rest that I go to than I have ever known." — A Tale of Two Cities.
"...and was soon borne away by the waves and lost in darkness and distance." — Frankenstein.
"...her full nature spent itself in channels which had no great name on the earth." — Middlemarch.
"...and yes I said yes I will Yes." — the soaring final words of Joyce's Ulysses.
A great last line echoes long after the book is shut. Which one stays with you?
